name: spotlight

frames.best_why: Frame 6 has the beam at its widest and brightest over the copy; earlier frames catch only its edge.

tagline: A cone of white light drifts down over a dark grid and settles on the headline.
summary: A near-black backdrop with a faint square grid and one soft diagonal beam of light that fades in and widens over the text below it. It is there to pull the eye to a single block of copy.
appearance: A near-black stage crossed by a faint square grid. A wide, soft white cone of light enters from the top-left and falls diagonally across the middle, brightest and broadest over the centred white headline and the small grey paragraph under it.
behaviour: On load an oversized blurred ellipse fades in and slides down-left for about two seconds, growing into the beam, then holds still. It does not follow the pointer; the sweep happens once.
demo_content: Headline "Spotlight is the new trend." with a short paragraph about drawing attention to text.
search_phrases: beam of light behind a headline
radial glow that draws the eye
subtle light sweep across a banner
animated backdrop for landing page text
stage light effect for website header
use_when: A dark page needs to hint at a focal line of copy without adding a heavy or looping animation.
avoid_when: You need the glow to track the cursor, or a light theme: it is fixed white on black.
customise: Only className and fill are exposed. Size, position, opacity and the one-shot sweep live in the source and its inline keyframes.
weight_why: One static SVG ellipse under a blur filter and a single CSS fade on load.

a11y.note: The decorative SVG is not marked aria-hidden and the load sweep ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

issues: Catalogue calls it mouse-tracked, but the code plays one fixed CSS keyframe and ignores the pointer.
polish_why: Clean beam and grid, but the single white glow does nothing after its load sweep.
